# Open statements of the single proof

<!-- Generated by scripts/one_proof/render_open.py from open-statements.json (the Lean build), kinds.tsv,
claims.tsv, reviews.tsv, credits.tsv and issues.json. Do not edit by hand: edit those, or regenerate the JSON
after a fold. -->

`ZInQ.OneProof.frozenTarget` (`ZInQKernel/OneProof/Main.lean`) is a Lean theorem, checked by the kernel with no
`sorry` and only the standard axioms, that proves the frozen target `ZInQ.FrozenTarget`, the theorem that Z is
Diophantine in Q (the 11/5 manuscript, Theorem 1.1), from the hypotheses below. Everything else is proved.
Each hypothesis is a Lean `Prop`; proving one in Lean, or reducing it to statements printed in the literature,
removes it. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to contribute and check a proof.

**43 hypotheses of the H part** (in the bundles `OpenAddedLeaves17`, `OpenResearchLeaves26`, `OpenTextbookLeaves12`), plus 11 hypotheses of the Tian–Yuan–Zhang and Gross–Zagier parts listed at the end.

* **Strict count: 33 published / 10 glue** (the strictest flagged reading; no hypothesis carries a strictest-reading flag).
* LEAF means a published, refereed theorem stated over genuine definitions in its printed form, or a direct
  instance of it (a special case that needs no argument). GLUE is everything else: a consequence of one theorem,
  a composite of several, project glue, or a leaf whose published form is still pending a reading (`kinds.tsv`,
  column `flag`).
* By kind: composite 3, consequence 7, published 33.

## How to help

* **Prove a statement in Lean**: pick a row whose status is open or "project interest, free to claim", claim
  it on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14) with a line `Claiming <field> at <commit>`
  (the field name as in the first column), and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
* **Check a statement against its printed source** (no Lean needed): pick a packet below and follow
  [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md). [pages-wanted.md](pages-wanted.md) lists the printed pages a
  reader can check.
* Tiers come from a model triage that no person has reviewed yet; treat them as a rough guide.
* The project logs its folds and landings on [issue #3](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/3).

## Good first targets

None at the moment.

## Held

A hypothesis is held only by a public claim line, on the claims issue or in a draft pull request that links it
(the project's own holds may point at a pushed branch). A claim with no public activity for 14 days gets one
ping, and is released if there is no reply within 7 days of the ping.

## Packets

A packet is a set of statements decided by reading one block of the literature. Claim a packet with a line
`Claiming reading <packet>` on its own issue if it has one, otherwise on the statement-checks issue, and until that issue is opened on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14); see [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md).

### Packet R1

Reduction block: SGA 7 I Exp. IX, BLR 1.2 Prop. 4, Serre-Tate 1968. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`r7a`](#r7a) (LEAF): Serre-Tate 1968 Thm 1
* [`raynaudSemistableSH`](#raynaudsemistablesh) (LEAF; reading-risk, unverified-locator): SGA 7 I Exp. IX Prop. 4.7 (Raynaud's criterion) over a strictly henselian DVR: m >= 3 invertible in O and A[m] rational over K imply semistable Neron models at O (number UNVERIFIED); with strictHenselizationPair gives the general-DVR 4.7 and, by K1 (Mumford 4 and [m] etale), 3.6

### Packet R2

Unread locators: SGA 3, EGA IV, Faltings 1983 Lemma 5, GIT, BLR 1.4, 7.2, 7.3. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`mumfordGroupLaw`](#mumfordgrouplaw) (LEAF; pending-review): Mumford-Fogarty-Kirwan, Geometric Invariant Theory, Thm 6.14 (S connected locally noetherian, F -> S smooth proper with a section e, a fibre an abelian variety: F is an abelian scheme with identity e), on each connected component; numbers UNVERIFIED
* [`sga3_VIB_3_10`](#sga3_vib_3_10) (LEAF; unverified-locator): SGA 3 VI_B 3.10 (number UNVERIFIED)
* [`neronSchemeExtensionExists`](#neronschemeextensionexists) (LEAF): BLR 1.4 Thm 3

### Packet R3

Tian-Yuan-Zhang and Gross-Zagier. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`h11`](#h11) (LEAF; unverified-locator): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Thm 1.1, first assertion, for odd m (arXiv:1411.4728v1 L371-380; journal number UNVERIFIED)
* [`hL3s`](#hl3s) (LEAF; unread, unverified-locator): Legendre, Essai sur la theorie des nombres (1798); Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801) art. 291-292 (article numbers UNVERIFIED); cited by TYZ arXiv:1411.4728v1 L533; not in Mathlib 4.35
* [`hJP`](#hjp) (LEAF; restricted, unread, unverified-locator): TYZ arXiv:1411.4728v1 L533, citing Jones-Pall, Regular and semi-regular positive ternary quadratic forms, Acta Math. 70 (1939) 165-191, Theorem 5 (not read, no network); checked exhaustively to 10^6 (h29-fix regular_form.py)
* [`hfx`](#hfx) (LEAF; restricted, unread): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), arXiv:1411.4728v1 section 2.1 (L542-550), Lemma 2.5, Theorem 2.4(1), Theorem 2.6 at chi = 1 (L809-840)
* [`hL29`](#hl29) (LEAF; restricted, unread): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), arXiv:1411.4728v1 Lemma 2.9 (L1062-1066)
* [`hT21`](#ht21) (LEAF; restricted, unread): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), arXiv:1411.4728v1 Theorem 2.1 (L554-559)
* [`hP23`](#hp23) (LEAF; restricted, unread): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), arXiv:1411.4728v1 Proposition 2.3 (L580-586)
* [`hCM`](#hcm) (GLUE; unverified-locator): Shimura 1971 (Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions) Thm 5.4, Shimura's reciprocity law at CM points, in idelic form (number UNVERIFIED)
* [`h33`](#h33) (LEAF): Tian-Yuan-Zhang, Thm 3.3 (Gross-Zagier formula), printed form for n = 5, 7 (mod 8) (arXiv:1411.4728v1 L1299-1311)
* [`hFH`](#hfh) (GLUE; pending-reading): Friedberg-Hoffstein, Ann. of Math. 142 (1995), Thm B, specialized to weight-2 newforms of trivial nebentypus and chi_0 = chi_D0 unramified at S containing the primes dividing 2N (gz-fh; locator UNVERIFIED)
* [`hL3`](#hl3) (GLUE): Gross-Zagier, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), Thm I.6.3 and Ch. V, with Gross's conjugation relation (Gross 1984, section 5)

### Packet R4

The discriminant-6 Shimura curve. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`gonzalezRotgerX6Ab`](#gonzalezrotgerx6ab) (LEAF; unverified-locator): Gonzalez-Rotger 2006 on X6 (printed form; locator UNVERIFIED)

### Packet R5

Heights. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`bostLowerBound`](#bostlowerbound) (LEAF; unverified-locator): Bost, Sem. Bourbaki 795 (Asterisque 237, 1996): h_D(A) >= -(g/2) log 2pi, Deligne normalization (display UNVERIFIED, height-split §2)
* [`javanpeykarBound`](#javanpeykarbound) (LEAF): Javanpeykar, Algebra Number Theory 8 (2014) Thm 1.1.1 (read by the audit), for curves over K with a K-rational Belyi function, over the published stable height
* [`pazukiCor13Upper`](#pazukicor13upper) (LEAF): Pazuki, Bull. SMF 140 (2012) Cor. 1.3(2), upper half (read by the audit; RISK: Pazuki's level-2 coordinates, height-split §8)
* [`gaudronRemondThm14`](#gaudronremondthm14) (LEAF): Gaudron-Remond, Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) Thm 1.4 (read by the audit), over the published stable height

### Packet R7

p-adic Hodge theory and modular Galois representations. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`r9a`](#r9a) (LEAF): Faltings 1983 Satz 3
* [`r9b`](#r9b) (LEAF): Faltings 1983 Satz 4, Kor. 1
* [`hodgeTateDecompAbVar`](#hodgetatedecompabvar) (LEAF): C_p (x) V_p(A) = C_p(1)^g + C_p^g, G_F-equivariant (Fontaine, Invent. Math. 65 (1982); Tate 1967 4; Faltings 1988), bases of the two g-dimensional spaces chosen
* [`deRhamH1AbVarT`](#derhamh1abvart) (LEAF): H^1_et(A_Fbar, Q_p), written Hom(V_p A, Q_p), is de Rham with the printed D_dR (Faltings 1989; Tsuji 1999; Scholze 2013 Cor. 1.8, wording read by h-leaves)
* [`r11r12`](#r11r12) (GLUE): Pan 2022 Thm 1.0.4 with Berger 2002 Thm 0.7 (not splittable: no B_st in Mathlib, hodge-split)
* [`eigenformHTNew`](#eigenformhtnew) (GLUE): Kato 2004 9.2-9.4 for newforms, transported to any semisimple attached rho and dualized (Kato's V_f not definable in Mathlib)
* [`dsThm966`](#dsthm966) (LEAF): Deligne-Serre 1974 Thm 4.1; Diamond-Shurman Thm 9.6.6 (k = 1, continuous, finite image)
* [`dsThm965Weak`](#dsthm965weak) (LEAF; unverified-locator): Diamond-Shurman, GTM 228, Thm 9.6.5 (Deligne 1971; Shimura 1971 Thm 7.14 for k = 2), weakest reading: rho(Frob_p) satisfies x^2 - a_p x + chi(p) p^(k-1); coefficients extended along iota_L o iota_C^-1
* [`tateTwistInvariants`](#tatetwistinvariants) (LEAF): C_p(i)^{G_K} = 0 for i != 0, K finite over Q_p in Qbar_p: Tate, p-divisible groups (1967) 3.3 Thm 2
* [`axSenTate`](#axsentate) (LEAF): C_p^{G_K} = K: Tate 1967 3.3 Thm 1; Sen 1969; Ax 1970

### Packet R10

Picard scheme and Weil pairing. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`picRepresentableAbVar`](#picrepresentableabvar) (LEAF; pending-review): Murre 1964, Oort 1962 (BLR Neron Models 8.2 Thm 3, number UNVERIFIED: Pic_{X/k} representable for X proper over a field, Pic as the fppf sheafification); dictionary pass 11-16: Murre-Oort is the print; the Kleiman 9.4.8 route would need projectivity and 9.2.5 (a consequence), so Murre-Oort is cited first. Earlier source text: Murre 1964, Oort 1962; FGA Exp. 232 Thm 3.1; Kleiman, The Picard scheme, Thm 9.4.8 with 9.2.5 (section 0): the relative Picard fppf sheaf of an abelian variety over a field is representable (locators UNVERIFIED)
* [`picZeroAbVar`](#piczeroabvar) (GLUE; unverified-locator): Mumford, Abelian varieties, 13; Kleiman, The Picard scheme, Prop. 9.5.1 and 9.5.3; Milne 1986, 9-10: the identity component of Pic_{A/K} is an abelian variety (locators UNVERIFIED)
* [`phiAmpleIsogeny`](#phiampleisogeny) (GLUE; unverified-locator): Mumford, Abelian varieties, 6 Application 1 and 8 Thm 1: for ample L, phi_L : A -> Pic0 is an isogeny (locators UNVERIFIED)
* [`weilPairingMumford`](#weilpairingmumford) (GLUE; unverified-locator): Mumford, Abelian varieties, 20 and 23; Milne 1986, Lemma 16.2(c) and 16: Mumford's pairing e_n : A[n] x Pic0[n] -> mu_n (locators UNVERIFIED)

### milneIsogenyQuasiInverse

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves17.milneIsogenyQuasiInverse`; kind **published**, strict **LEAF**.
* Source: fg = [d], gf = [d] as morphisms: Milne 1986 Rem. 8.4; Milne's notes Prop. 7.1; Mumford 7
* label project-interest (project interest, free to claim); tier T2 (model triage, unreviewed); discussion: [elliotglazer #81](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/issues/81).
* Human readings recorded: none.

```lean
AvSplit.MilneIsogenyQuasiInverse
```

> **LEAF (H-54; published form).** Milne, *Abelian varieties*, in Cornell–Silverman (eds.),
> *Arithmetic Geometry* (1986), §8, Remark 8.4 (UNVERIFIED number; also Milne's online notes
> *Abelian Varieties* (2008), Prop. 7.1 / Rem. 7.3, UNVERIFIED): "for an isogeny `f : A → B` of
> degree `n` there is an isogeny `g : B → A` with `g ∘ f = n_A` and `f ∘ g = n_B`", over any field.
> Specialization read off the same display: the degree `n` is weakened to "some `d ≥ 1`", the
> conclusion "`g` is an isogeny" is dropped, and the hypothesis "isogeny" is given as "finite and
> surjective" (`IsIsogenyMor`), which implies Milne's "surjective with finite kernel" (the kernel is
> the base change of the finite `f` along the zero section). `[d]_A` is `((d : ℤ) : End A)`, the
> `d`-fold sum of the identity in `Hom(A, A)`. Over an algebraically closed field this is also
> Mumford, *Abelian varieties* (1970), §7, Remark after Thm 4 (UNVERIFIED).

```

> **LEAF (H-25; published form).** Mumford, *Abelian varieties* (1970; 2nd ed. 1974), §4,
> Application 2, (iv) (UNVERIFIED locator): for an abelian variety `X` of dimension `g` over an
> algebraically closed field `k` and an integer `n` with `char k ∤ n`, the group
> `X_n = {x ∈ X : nx = 0}` of `n`-torsion points is isomorphic to `(ℤ/nℤ)^{2g}`. Mumford's points
> are the closed points, i.e. the `k`-points (`Pts A k`); `dim` is the topological Krull dimension
> of the underlying space; "`char k ∤ n`" with `n ≥ 1` is `(n : k) ≠ 0`; the group isomorphism is a
> bijection `e` with `e(x + y) = e x + e y` (written multiplicatively on points).

> (UNVERIFIED locator; over any field): for an abelian subvariety `B` of an abelian variety `J`

> (UNVERIFIED locator: `B ∩ Z` finite and `B + Z = J`). Stated here with "abelian subvariety" as a
> homomorphism `i : B → J` that is a closed immersion, in characteristic `0`, and without the
> conclusion that `g : Z → J` is a closed immersion (so weaker than the published statement).

> **LEAF SHIMURA-5.4 (the main theorem of complex multiplication, with torsion; printed form in
> Weierstrass coordinates).** Let `K = ℚ(√−m) ⊂ ℂ` (through `κ`, `√−m ↦ i√m`), `e : Kˢ → ℚ̄`
> normalized (`ιC ∘ e = κ` on `K`), `σ ∈ Aut(ℂ)` and `s ∈ 𝔸_K^×` with `σ = [s, K]` on `K^ab`
> (`ArtinCond`). Let `𝔞 ⊂ K` be a lattice, `P` a period pair with lattice `κ(𝔞)` and `P'` one with
> lattice `κ(s⁻¹𝔞)`. Then there is `μ ∈ ℂˣ` such that `(x, y) ↦ (μ⁻²x, μ⁻³y)` is an isomorphism
> `E_P^σ ≅ E_{P'}` (`σ(g₂(P)) = μ⁴g₂(P')`, `σ(g₃(P)) = μ⁶g₃(P')`) and, for `u ∈ K \ 𝔞` and any
> `v ∈ K` representing `s⁻¹u ∈ K/s⁻¹𝔞` (`s_f v − u ∈ 𝔞̂`),
> `σ(℘_P(u)) = μ²℘_{P'}(v)` and `σ(℘'_P(u)) = μ³℘'_{P'}(v)`.
> 
> Source: Shimura 1971, *Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions*, Thm. 5.4:
> for an analytic isomorphism `ξ : ℂ/𝔞 → E(ℂ)` there is a unique `ξ' : ℂ/s⁻¹𝔞 → E^σ(ℂ)` with
> `ξ(u)^σ = ξ'(s⁻¹u)` for all `u ∈ K/𝔞`; Lang, *Elliptic functions*, Ch. 10, Thm. 3; Silverman,
> *Advanced topics*, GTM 151, Thm. II.8.2 (for `𝒪_K`) (theorem numbers UNVERIFIED, from memory).
> Here `E = E_P : y² = 4x³ − g₂(P)x − g₃(P)` with `ξ = (℘_P, ℘'_P)`; every analytic isomorphism
> `ℂ/s⁻¹𝔞 → E^σ(ℂ)` is `z ↦ (μ²℘_{P'}(z), μ³℘'_{P'}(z))` for some `μ ∈ ℂˣ` (`ξ'(0) = ξ(0)^σ = O`,
> a holomorphic map of complex tori fixing `0` is `z ↦ αz`, and isomorphisms of short Weierstrass
> models are `(x, y) ↦ (μ²x, μ³y)`), so this is the printed statement, restricted to `u ∉ 𝔞` (then
> `v ∉ s⁻¹𝔞`, since `K ∩ 𝔞̂ = 𝔞`, so `℘_{P'}(v)` is a value, not the junk value at a pole); the
> conclusion holds for every representative `v` because two of them differ by an element of `s⁻¹𝔞`. Normalization:
> Shimura's `[s, K]` sends a uniformizer at `𝔭` to the arithmetic Frobenius, as Tau Ceti's Artin map
> does; then `E^{Frob_𝔭} ≅ ℂ/𝔭⁻¹𝔞`, consistent with `j(𝔞)^{Art 𝔭} = j(𝔭⁻¹𝔞)` used by the kernel's
> `MainTheoremCMj` (Tau Ceti: `globalArtinMap_isArithFrobAt`, `isArithFrobAt_of_globalArtinMap_ofAdicCompletion_eq`;
> re-check this direction if the Artin map is ever replaced). The Weierstrass-coordinate form is a standard consequence
> of Thm. 5.4; Silverman's II.8.2 covers only `𝒪_K`, while this leaf quantifies over lattices of every order.

> **Leaf TYZ-3.3: TYZ Theorem 3.3 ("Gross–Zagier formula"), printed form, for `n ≡ 5, 7 (mod 8)`.**
> 
> Source: Tian–Yuan–Zhang, *Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem*,
> arXiv:1411.4728v1 (Asian J. Math. 21 (2017) 721–774), Theorem 3.3 (`\label{GZ}`, Period7.tex
> L1299–1311), with the definitions of §3.1: `Cl_n = Gal(H_n/K_n)`, `Cl'_n`, `σ` (L1263–1265), `Φ` and
> `P_χ` (L1279–1284), `𝒫(n) = 2^{−1−ρ(n)} 𝓛(n) α_n ∈ A(K_n)^- ⊗ ℚ` (L1288–1295), `h₂` (L992). The
> statement, for every positive squarefree `n ≡ 5, 7 (mod 8)`, every `Φ` and every character
> `χ : Cl_n → {±1}`:
> 
> * `P_χ` is non-torsion only if `χ = χ_{d₀,d₁}` with `n = d₀d₁`, `0 < d₀ ≡ 5, 6, 7`,
> `0 < d₁ ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)` (the character of `K_n(√d₁)`, resp. `K_n(√d₁*)` for `n ≡ 7`);
> * in that case `P_χ = ε(d₀,d₁) 2^{h₂(n)} 𝓛(d₁) 𝒫(d₀)` in `A(H'_n(i)) ⊗ ℚ`, `ε(d₀,d₁) = ±i` on
> `(5,3)`, `±1` otherwise.
> 
> Encoding (a reading of the same display, never stronger):
> * Model: the leaf is stated over the kernel's `basePt`, i.e. Heegner points on the eta-quotient model
> `X0.phiC`, whereas TYZ build `z_n` from an arbitrary identification `i_0`. Passing from the print to the
> leaf uses that the eta-model coordinates are rational functions on `X₀(32)` (q-expansion principle;
> `IsRatModFn 32` in Bridge.lean), so `phiC = [M]∘i_0` with `M ∈ End_ℚ(A) = ℤ`, which the existential
> `𝒫` absorbs. So the leaf is TYZ Theorem 3.3 carried along the eta model, not its literal display
> (statement review v2, M1).
> * `A(H'_n(i)) ⊗ ℚ ⊂ A(ℚ̄) ⊗ ℚ`; a vector of `A(ℚ̄) ⊗ ℚ` is `Q/m`; equality is "the difference of the
> cleared multiples is torsion". `A` is the kernel's `y² = x³ + 4x ≅ X₀(32)`, `ℚ`-isomorphic to TYZ's
> `2y² = x³ + x` by `(x, y) ↦ (2x, 4y)`, compatibly with `[i]`; `z_n = f_n(P_n)` is the kernel's
> pinned point `TYZ35.basePt n` (cm-numeric/cm-bridge; `(1 − [i]) f₀(P_n)` for `n ≡ 5`). TYZ print
> `f_n = f₀ − f₀∘[i]` (L1196) with `[i]` an automorphism of `X_U ≅ X₀(32)_{ℚ(i)}`; reading it as
> `(1 − [i])∘f₀` with this sign of `i` is fixed by the paper: in the proof of the Hecke-action
> proposition for `n ≡ 5` the cusps `[∞,1]`, `[0]` lie on the component of `P_n` and `α = −i`
> (about L1238, L1519, L1551, L1564-1566), so TYZ's `[i]` acts as `+i` there; with this sign
> `f_n = f₀∘[1 − i]` (about L1584) is `ϖ`-invariant up to 2-torsion (about L1586-1589), as Prop. 3.1
> and the proof of Thm 3.3 (about L1909-1912) need. It agrees with cm-numeric's numerics. With the
> other sign the lifts do not commute with `[i]`, the contributing and excluded characters swap,
> and the leaf would be false, not weaker (statement review of tyz-split, 2026-11-14).
> * Non-vacuity: the hypothesis on `ℓ` is satisfiable only if every `𝓛(m)²` (`m ≡ 1, 3`) is an integer
> square, i.e. together with `TYZThm11Integral` (TYZ Thm 1.1); otherwise the leaf (and the row,
> through `IsTYZLcal`) is vacuously true.
> * `h₂` is defined in TYZ §2 (L992) and reused in §3 (L2354).
> * `𝒫(d)` enters only through `Q d / m d` with `Q d ∈ A(K_d)^-` and `Q d` torsion when
> `ord_{s=1} L(E_d, s) > 1` (then `𝓛(d) = 0` by its definition, L338–345, so `𝒫(d) = 0`, L1295).
> This forgets the value `2^{−1−ρ(d)}𝓛(d)` of the coefficient (it needs Néron–Tate regulators,
> not in Mathlib): the leaf is weaker than the printed theorem, not stronger.
> * `𝓛(d₁)` (`d₁ ≡ 1, 3`, `n` odd) is defined up to sign (L364); `ℓ` is any integer choice with
> `ℓ(d₁)² = 𝓛(d₁)²` (`lcalSq`), the sign absorbed in `ε` (`ε` is chosen after `ℓ`).
> * Only `n ≡ 5, 7` (TYZ: `n ≡ 5, 6, 7`); then `d₀, d₁` are odd, so the classes `6, 2` do not occur
> (they are kept in the statement as printed).
> * `Φ` is encoded by lifts (`IsPhi`), `χ` is a character of `Cl_n = Gal(H_n/K_n)` itself.

> **Friedberg–Hoffstein, Theorem B, with `ε(½, π ⊗ χ₀) = 1` written as the functional equation of
> `Λ(f ⊗ χ_{D₀}, s)` with sign `+1`.** As `FriedbergHoffsteinB`, except that the compatibility
> hypothesis reads: the entire continuation `G` of `L(f ⊗ χ_{D₀}, s) = ∑ aₙ(f) χ_{D₀}(n) n^{−s}`
> satisfies `Λ(2 − s) = Λ(s)` on `0 < Re s < 2`, where
> `Λ(s) = (N D₀²)^{s/2} (2π)^{−s} Γ(s) G(s)` (`ZInQ.Literature.completedL`). For `(D₀, N) = 1`
> (forced by `p ∤ D₀` for `p ∈ S ⊇ {p ∣ N}`) the conductor of `π_f ⊗ χ₀` is `N D₀²`, its completed
> L-function satisfies `Λ(2 − s) = ε(½, π ⊗ χ₀) Λ(s)`, and `Λ ≢ 0` on the strip (since `G ≢ 0`, as
> `a₁ = 1`), so the hypothesis says exactly `ε(½, π ⊗ χ₀) = 1`. The strip avoids the junk values of
> Mathlib's `Complex.Gamma` at the poles (as in `ZInQ.Literature.FunctionalEquation5`).
> 
> Source: Friedberg–Hoffstein, Ann. of Math. (2) 142 (1995) 385–423, Theorem B (UNVERIFIED; see
> `FriedbergHoffsteinB` for the dictionary and the open checks).

* packet [R3](#packet-r3); label long-pole (statement checks first; Lean only at Mathlib scale); tier T4 (model triage, unreviewed); discussion: [elliotglazer #76](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/issues/76).

ZInQ.GZDecomp.GrossZagierHeegner
```

> **(L3) Gross–Zagier with Gross's conjugation relation, in the form that can be stated today.**
> Let `E/ℚ` be an elliptic curve whose L-series is that of a weight-2 newform `f` of level `N` and
> trivial nebentypus (`aₙ(f) = aₙ(E)` for all `n ≥ 1`). Let `D < −4` be an odd fundamental
> discriminant with the Heegner hypothesis for `N`, and suppose `L(f, s)` has a simple zero at
> `s = 1` while `L(f ⊗ χ_D, 1) ≠ 0` (so `L'(E/K, 1) = L'(f, 1) L(f ⊗ χ_D, 1) ≠ 0`). Then for every
> field `K ≅ ℚ(√D)` the group `E(K)` has a point `y` of infinite order (the Heegner point `y_K`)
> with `σ y − y` torsion for every `σ ∈ Aut(K/ℚ)` (`ȳ_K = −ε y_K` up to torsion, `ε = −1`).
> 
> Literature: B. Gross, D. Zagier, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), 225-320, Theorem I.6.3 and its
> corollaries in Ch. V (UNVERIFIED numbers): `L'(E/K, 1) = c ĥ(y_K)` with `c ≠ 0`; B. Gross,
> *Heegner points on X₀(N)*, Modular forms (Durham 1983), 1984, for `ȳ_K = −ε y_K` mod torsion
> (UNVERIFIED). Folded in, because the modular curve `X₀(N)`, the parametrization and the Heegner
> point cannot be stated in Lean today: the modular parametrization `X₀(N) → E` (Eichler–Shimura
> construction of the strong Weil curve `E_f`, Shimura 1971, Thm 7.14-7.15, UNVERIFIED, plus
> Faltings 1983 Korollar 2 (`L(E) = L(E_f)` ⇒ `E ∼ E_f`), or for CM curves Shimura, Nagoya Math. J.
> 43 (1971)); and nondegeneracy of `ĥ` on `E(K)` (proved in Tau Ceti:
> `Affine.Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder`).
